﴿Rivalry for more diverts you.﴾ This is a statement intended as admonition and reproach. The meaning of "diverts you" is that it preoccupies you. "Rivalry" (al-takathur) is boasting about the abundance of wealth and children, and each group saying: "We are more numerous," and the other saying: "We are more numerous." When the Prophet (ﷺ) recited it, he said: "The son of Adam says: 'My wealth, my wealth.' Yet you have no portion of your wealth except what you have eaten and consumed, what you have worn and worn out, or what you have given in charity and sent forward."

﴿Until you visit the graves.﴾ There are three opinions on this. The first: its meaning is "until you die," so that visiting the graves means being buried in them. The second: its meaning is "until you remember the dead who are in the graves," so visiting them is expressed as boasting about those who are in them, because some Arabs boasted of their dead ancestors. The meaning then is: "Rivalry for more diverts you until you reach the point of mentioning the dead." The third: its meaning is literal visiting of the graves, to honour their occupants and to boast of them, saying: "This is the grave of so-and-so," in order to make his name famous and magnify his rank.

﴿No! You will come to know.﴾ This is a rebuke and a threat. He repeated it for emphasis and joined it with "then" (thumma) to indicate that the second is greater than the first. It has been said: the first is a threat to the disbelievers and the second is a threat to the believers. The object of "you will know" is omitted, and its implied sense is "what will befall you," or "you will know that the Qur'an is true," or "you will know that you were in error in your preoccupation with this world." It was omitted for the purpose of inspiring awe, so that the listener imagines the greatest thing that comes to his mind.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 102, verses 5–8:

﴿Had you known with certainty of knowledge﴾: the answer to "law" (lo, "if") is omitted, its estimated form being: "Had you known, you would have been restrained and prepared yourselves for the Hereafter." Therefore it is proper to pause at "al-yaqin" (certainty). The object of "to know" (ta'lamun) in "law ta'lamun" is also omitted. "ilm al-yaqin" (knowledge of certainty) is a verbal noun (masdar). The meaning of "ilm al-yaqin" is: the knowledge about which there is no doubt. Some of them said: it is of the type of an attribute added to its own noun, like your saying "dar al-akhirah" (the abode of the Hereafter). Al-Zamakhshari said: its meaning is the knowledge of the matters that you are certain of through direct observation. ﴿Surely you will see the Hellfire﴾: this is the answer to an omitted oath, and it explains the object of "law ta'lamun," its estimated form being: "Had you known the outcome of your affair," then he explained it as being the seeing of the Hellfire. Explanation after ambiguity indicates awe and magnification. The address is to all people, and it is like His saying: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾ [Maryam: 71]. It was also said: it is specifically for the disbelievers, so "seeing" in this case is intended to mean entering it. ﴿Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾: this is an emphasis of the earlier seeing, and its being joined with "thumma" (then) is for awe and magnification. "Ayn" (the eye) here is from your saying: "ayn al-shay'" (the very self and essence of a thing), meaning: you will see it with the sight that is the very essence of certainty. ﴿Then you will surely be asked on that Day about the bounty﴾: this is information about being questioned in the Hereafter about the blessings of the world. It was said: the bounty is security and health; it was said: food and drink. These are examples, and the correct view is generality, covering everything that one takes pleasure in. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A house that shelters you, a garment that covers you, and a morsel that keeps your heart firm; whatever is beyond that is bounty." He (ﷺ) also said: "Every bounty will be questioned about, except the bounty in the way of Allah." One day the Prophet (ﷺ) ate fresh dates with his Companions and they drank water after it, and he said to them: "This is from the bounty about which you will be questioned."
